newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks still bullish in record trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks still bullish in record trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks continued their early charge and had receded marginally from new intraday records at midday trade on Thursday due to what dealers said was a heavy inflow of foreign capital.
"There's a lot of foreign buyers in the market, as has been the case for several days now. We've seen a string of positive economic news and it's a bull market" a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 54.96 points, or 1.28 percent, at 4,336.48, or just shy of a trading record of 4,338.21 set minutes earlier.
Brisk trading volume of 75.8 million shares confirmed the presence of foreign as well as domestic buyers, traders said.
"They're buying across the board, only financials have gone off the boil a little," a desk trader said.
Financial stock Bancomer and telecomms firm Telmex continued to drive the market.
Bancomer A shares were ahead 1 centavo to 2.19 pesos, although their B shares had shed earlier gains to stand unchanged at 3.82 pesos.
Telmex had climbed 28 centavos to 18.80 pesos, shadowing its ADRs which were up 1/2 to 47-1/4 on Wall Street. The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 47.50 points to 7,763.49.
Dealers said cement stocks were trading strongly, due to a combination of recommendations and a strong performance by the construction industry reported in Tuesday's industrial output data.
Cement firm Cemex was up 60 centavos to 32.85 pesos, while its counterpart Apasco had gained 1.50 pesos to 53.10 pesos.
Lazard Freres and Co. earlier announced they had begun coverage of Cemex with a buy recommendation, and of Apasco as hold.
On the broad market, of 11 stocks traded in total, gainers far outpaced sliders, by 72 to 15.
